title: word2vec

gpu_support.notes: `word2vec` looks up host-resident text/model metadata and returns a numeric matrix; it does not use provider kernels.

description: `word2vec(emb, words)` returns one embedding-vector row per requested word from a RunMat `wordEmbedding` object.
behaviors: `emb` must be a RunMat `wordEmbedding` compatibility object, normally created by `readWordEmbedding`.
`words` may be a string scalar, string array, character vector, character matrix, or cell array of scalar text.
The output is an `n`-by-`emb.Dimension` numeric matrix, where `n` is the number of requested words after flattening the input text container.
Words missing from the vocabulary return `NaN` rows.
`word2vec(___, 'IgnoreCase', true)` performs case-insensitive vocabulary lookup and uses the first matching vocabulary entry.

faqs.question: What happens for missing words?
faqs.answer: RunMat returns a row of `NaN` values for each missing vocabulary word.

faqs.question: Does `word2vec` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It is a host lookup into a text model object.

example.input:
M = word2vec(emb, words)
M = word2vec(emb, words, 'IgnoreCase', true)
example.output: `M` is a numeric matrix with one row per input word.

points: Input words are flattened into lookup order.

gpu_residency: `word2vec` reads host model metadata and returns a CPU numeric matrix.
